newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japanese bank sells part of Softbank holding.
newsitem.headline: Big Japanese bank sells part of Softbank holding.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan said Monday it sold part of its stake in personal computer software wholesaler Softbank Corp.

IBJ denied a weekend report in business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun that said it planned to sell all of its Softbank holdings by March 31, but the article nevertheless helped push the stock down by 330 yen (nearly $3) to 9,970 yen ($89) in Monday trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

The newspaper said the reason for IBJ's sale was that Softbank had been relying more on the capital market and short-term bank loans to fund its aggressive expansion than on IBJ, one of Japan's three long-term credit banks.

A Softbank spokesman said IBJ had sold 220,000 shares, worth five billion yen ($45.0 million), in June, lowering its stake to 0.4 percent, against 0.9 percent at the end of March. The bank now owns 223,000 Softbank shares, he said.
Although IBJ held less than a 1 percent stake in Softbank before the sale, it was one of its main shareholders.
An IBJ spokesman confirmed the bank had sold part of its holding this year but declined to why or how many shares it had sold.

The Softbank spokesman said the shares were purchased by a Softbank group company. "The fact that we are reducing our business ties with the bank could be one reason for the bank's sale of our shares," he said.
"Since we publicly offered our shares in July 1994, our short-term demand for funds has been covered by bank loans and our long-term demand by funds raised from the capital market," he added.
As of Sept. 30, the major shareholders in Softbank were president Masayoshi Son, with about 3 percent, and Son's asset management firm MAC Inc., with 47.85 percent.

Softbank is Japan's largest software distributor and has made a series of high-profile purchases or tie-ups. They include U.S. computer magazine publisher Ziff-Davis Publishing and tie-ups such companies as Australia's News Corp., Yahoo! Inc. and Sega Enterprises Ltd.
